parts.title: A winter in the Arctic
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last January, my aunt Mira flew to a small town in the north of Norway, where she works as a doctor for the winter. She sent us a long letter about her first week there.

The first thing she noticed was the darkness. For two months, the sun does not rise at all, and the town is lit only by street lamps and a blue light from the sky at midday. At first she felt sleepy all the time, but the local people gave her some advice: go out every day, eat fish and take a vitamin tablet.

She also had to learn to dress properly. "Wear three thin layers rather than one thick one," a neighbour told her. "Your own warmth stays between them." She laughed, but when she went out with just a coat, she was freezing within five minutes.

The best part, she writes, was the northern lights. One night, the sky turned green and then pink, and it moved like a ribbon. She stood in the snow for an hour and forgot the cold. She says she will come back next winter.

parts.title: Why is ice important?
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Ice covers about ten percent of the land on our planet. Most of it is found at the two poles, in the Arctic and in Antarctica. [1] Without it, the world would be a very different place.

First, ice helps to keep the Earth cool. Its white surface sends the sun's light back into space. [2] When the ice melts, the dark water absorbs more heat, and this makes the planet warmer.

Second, ice stores fresh water. About two thirds of all the fresh water on Earth is frozen in glaciers. [3] Millions of people depend on rivers that begin high in the mountains.

Third, ice is the home of many animals. Polar bears hunt seals on the sea ice. [4] If the ice disappears, they will lose their food and their place to live.

Scientists are watching the ice very carefully. [5] They use satellites to measure how fast it is changing every year.
sentences: The Arctic is also much windier than most people expect.
This is a problem, because the bears cannot swim for ever.
It acts like a giant mirror at the top and bottom of the world.
They want to understand how it will change in the future.
Ice was once cut from lakes and sold to keep food fresh.
This water slowly melts in the summer and flows down into the valleys.
The ice in the poles is more than three kilometres thick in some places.
Ice is very useful to human beings, although most of us never see it.

gaps.explanation: Ice is useful to human beings, and the next sentence says the world would be different without it.
It acts like a giant mirror, which explains the white surface and the light going back into space.
The water melts in summer and flows down; the next sentence mentions rivers.
The bears cannot swim for ever, so losing the ice is a problem.
They want to understand the change, and the next sentence says they use satellites.

In the evening, we went to a hot spring, [4] was great after the cold day. I have taken hundreds of photographs, [5] I will show you when I come home. We are flying back on Sunday, and I [6] wait to tell you everything. Lots of love, Hannah

parts.title: Penguins
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they use their wings [1] swim, and they are excellent swimmers. They spend most of their lives in the sea, and they only come onto the ice to rest or to have babies. The emperor penguin is the largest kind. It can grow to over one metre, [2] it is also the only penguin that breeds in the winter. The father keeps the egg warm on his feet for two months, while the mother goes to the sea to find food. During this time, he does not eat [3] all. When the chick is born, the mother comes back. Penguins live close together in big groups, [4] helps them to stay warm in the freezing wind. They take turns standing in the middle, [5] is the warmest place. In this way, nobody has to stay outside the whole time. Scientists say that penguins are an example of how animals can work [6] a team.

gaps.explanation: Use their wings to swim: purpose.
It can grow over one metre, and it is also the only one that breeds in winter.
Does not eat at all: a fixed phrase.
A big group, which helps them stay warm: a relative clause.
The middle, which is the warmest place.
Work as a team: a role.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What was the temperature in Norway?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Minus twenty at night, but it felt warmer because there was no wind.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Minus twenty! I cannot imagine that. Was the sun out during the day?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: The sun was out for only three hours, and it did not give much heat. It felt warmer at night because there was no wind. When the wind blew, I felt much colder, even with my big coat.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What did you wear?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Three layers, wool socks, a hat and thick gloves. And a coat, of course, but the coat was not the reason it felt warm.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: How did you travel to the North Pole?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: By plane to the base, then by sledge pulled by dogs for three days.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Three days with dogs! That sounds amazing. Did you cross any water by boat?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: No, the ice was thick, so we did not need a boat. We did not go on skis either, except for the last hour. The dogs did all the work, and I sat on the sledge with a blanket.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Were the dogs friendly?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Very. They are like family to the guide. At night, they slept in the snow, and in the morning they were ready to run.

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Only one? How big was it? Did you take photos?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: It was huge, as big as a car. I took a lot of photos with my zoom lens, but the guide said not to open the window. I wanted to walk to the water and see it closer, but that is very dangerous.

turns.speaker: f

turns.text: I am scared of falling through the ice.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Do not worry. It is more than a metre thick, so it is very safe.

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: I have just heard that our trip to Iceland is cancelled.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: What a pity! I was looking forward to it so much.

turns.speaker: f

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: f

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Yes, let us do that. I will write to the company this evening.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Excuse me, could you tell me where the penguins are?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Go past the café, then turn left. You cannot miss them.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Thank you. I want to see them before the feeding time. Is it at three o'clock?

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Yes, at three. You will see the keepers with buckets of fish. It is the best time to go, because the penguins are very active, and they jump into the water.

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Are tickets cheaper in the afternoon? I am not hungry, so I do not want to eat in the café now.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: No, the ticket is the same price all day. But you can get a map at the entrance for free.

question.explanation: He asks where the penguins are, and she gives directions.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: My hands are freezing. Can we go inside for a while?

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: Of course. There is a hot chocolate stand next to the exit.

turns.speaker: f
turns.text: Great idea. I took off my gloves to take a photo, and now I cannot feel my fingers. I do not want to take any more photos today.

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: f

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: m
turns.text: I think I have lost my gloves. I left them on the bus.

turns.speaker: f

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: f

turns.speaker: m

turns.speaker: f

parts.title: A talk about Antarctica
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: nathalie
turns.text: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming. Please sit comfortably, because I have many photos to show you. I am Dr Eira Frost, and I spent eight months in Antarctica last year. I travelled there with a team of six scientists. It is the coldest, windiest and driest place on Earth. It is a desert, and it hardly ever rains or snows there. The lowest temperature ever recorded there was minus eighty-nine degrees. At that temperature, a cup of hot tea turns into ice in a few minutes. About thirty countries have research stations in Antarctica, but nobody lives there for ever. People stay for a few months or a year, and then they go home. In the summer, about five thousand scientists work there, but in winter, the number is only one thousand. At that time, the sun does not rise for several weeks, and it is dark almost all day. My job was to measure the thickness of the ice. This helps us understand how the climate of our planet is changing. Every week, I drove a snow vehicle for two hours to a special camp. We took samples from deep holes, and we wore thick suits and goggles. Life is simple at the station. We ate together, and in the evenings we watched films or played cards. Once a month, the cook made a big cake, and everyone had a party. The thing I missed most was fresh fruit, because it takes a long time to reach the base. The ship comes only twice a year, and the vegetables are usually frozen. I would love to go back one day, and I recommend it to anyone who loves adventure.

gaps.prompt: Dr Frost spent ___ months in Antarctica
gaps.explanation: I spent eight months in Antarctica.

gaps.prompt: The lowest recorded temperature was minus ___ degrees
gaps.explanation: The lowest temperature was minus eighty-nine degrees.
About thirty countries have research stations.
In winter the number is only one thousand.

gaps.prompt: Her job was to measure the thickness of the ___
gaps.explanation: My job was to measure the thickness of the ice.
The thing I missed most was fresh fruit.

parts.title: An interview with a polar guide
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Emrys, you take tourists to the Arctic. What do you enjoy most?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: The silence. When the engine stops, there is no sound except the wind and the ice moving. It is very peaceful.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How did you become a guide?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I was a sailor for ten years, and then I joined a small company that took tourists to Greenland. The first trip was so special that I never looked for another job.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Is your job dangerous?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: It can be. The weather changes quickly, and there are polar bears. That is why we always carry a radio and never go out alone.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you carry in your bag?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A radio, a first-aid kit, a map and a flask of tea. And chocolate, because it gives energy and makes people happy.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you tell visitors before a trip?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: To dress in layers and to drink a lot of water. People forget to drink when it is cold, and that makes them tired.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What do you eat on a trip?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A lot of soup, bread and cheese. The cook makes hot meals for everyone, and we have a big breakfast with porridge, because we need energy for the whole day.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Do you ever feel cold?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Of course, especially my toes. After twenty years I still need two pairs of socks. But I know how to dress, so the cold is not a problem.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Have you seen changes in the ice during your career?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Yes, many. Places where we used to walk are now open water. It makes me sad, but it also makes me want to teach people.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: How do tourists react to these changes?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Many are shocked when they see photos from twenty years ago. Some cry, others become angry. Most of them go home and tell their families, and that is important.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the funniest thing that has happened?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A seal once climbed onto our boat and fell asleep in the front. We waited an hour for it to leave.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What was your most beautiful day?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: A morning in March, when the northern lights were green, red and purple at the same time. Nobody spoke for ten minutes. It was like a dream.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What are your plans for the future?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: I am writing a book for children about life in the Arctic. I hope it will make young readers love the ice.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Would you like to live in a warmer place?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Never. I like the long winters and the quiet. But I love to visit my sister in Spain once a year, to feel the sun.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Thank you, Emrys. Is there a last message?

turns.speaker: h
turns.text: Take care of the ice. It does not belong only to the polar bears.

parts.title: Talk about the topic
parts.instructions: Answer the questions. Try to give a reason or an example with each answer.

questions.prompt: Do you think that we should protect the polar regions? Why?
Would you like to work as a scientist in a cold place? Why or why not?
What do you think life is like at a research station?
